analysis.title: Energy Futures: When Managed Money Brent Oil Selling Tops $6bn
key_insights: Managed Money Brent selling topped $6bn notional for only the 7th time in 5 years per CFTC Commitment of Traders. Managed Money sold $6.6bn from Oct 27 to Nov 3 alongside a 5.3% price drop, with liquidation ($4.9bn) the main driver.

The selling coincided with US and Iran signaling more willingness to pursue diplomacy, including President Trump reportedly choosing negotiations over strikes and Supreme Leader Khamenei granting the Iranian President authority for dialogue.

Recent history suggests flows stay challenged. Since Liberation Day there were 3 similar heavy-selling instances, and each was followed by 2 weeks of persistent negative activity, most notably after the initial Iran-US MOU in June 2026.

A longer lookback shows one swift reversal. Over May 28 to June 4, 2024, Managed Money sold $7.9bn on OPEC's scheduled end of voluntary output curbs. After OPEC ministers pushed back against the market reaction, Managed Money net length was fully restored.

The midterm elections prompted more long terminations. On Nov 4 the Democratic sweep raised expectations of constraints on President Trump's agenda, including funding for overseas military operations. Brent fell 8.7% and open interest shed $2.7bn.
Per GS Futures Strategists' CTA framework, short-term momentum turned negative on Nov 4 for the first time since August, unlocking additional systematic selling.

Price stabilized afterward. Brent recouped 3.9% on Nov 5 and 6, 3-month implied volatility richened, normalized 25 delta put-call skew cheapened, and calls were repurchased, which signals some bullish positioning in options.
risk_factors: Continued Managed Money selling, as 3 prior heavy-selling episodes since Liberation Day were each followed by about 2 weeks of negative flows.
Further US-Iran diplomatic progress could add downward pressure on Brent.
Midterm-driven political shifts could constrain US foreign policy and military funding, and prompt more long liquidation.
Negative CTA short-term momentum signal could trigger additional systematic selling.
